A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ReCon-GS and contain complete, readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Their content can be matched reliably despite appendix layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on N3DV, Meet Room, PanopticSports, and Technicolor, together with ablations and qualitative evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and analyses, including the benchmark results in Tables 1–3 and appendix evaluations.

M1.justification: The hierarchical motion representation, anchor assignment, hierarchy reconfiguration, deformation inheritance, and two-stage optimization remain unchanged. Table 12 documents density settings without changing the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same datasets and scenes: N3DV, Meet Room, PanopticSports, and Technicolor. No additional task, domain, or test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the benchmark tables, per-scene tables, and figures, including the HiCoM and 3DGStream comparisons. Table 12 contains only ReCon-GS configurations.

E3.justification: The reported metrics, training budgets, resolutions, and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Table 12 explicitly lists density settings for the existing trade-off analysis; it does not establish a revised evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The component, hierarchy-depth, training-step, initial-frame, temporal-degradation, and anchor-distribution analyses are retained. Table 12 details the already presented density/storage trade-off rather than introducing a distinct sensitivity or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results are averaged over three independent runs. No run-count revision, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-reporting changes appear.

E6.justification: Table 12 adds explicit density-indexed numerical entries, including 32.72 dB at 0.63 MB/frame for 1/16 density and 32.11 dB at 0.14 MB/frame for 1/96. Its PSNR sequence matches the existing Figure 1 curve, so this expands numerical reporting rather than demonstrating improved performance. Tables 1–11 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and formulations in Sections 3–4, including Equations 1–9, are unchanged. Neither version introduces additional theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims, including approximately 15% faster training and over 50% storage reduction at equivalent rendering quality.

C2.justification: The explanations of motion coherence, error accumulation, and storage efficiency are retained. Limitations concerning monocular or specialized reconstruction and abrupt object emergence or disappearance are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Table 12 newly specifies the density settings 1/16, 1/24, 1/32, 1/48, 1/64, and 1/96 associated with the reported trade-off. Existing implementation details, hardware, training schedules, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning, and all 53 reference entries are unchanged. The bibliography merely starts on a different page.

P1.justification: v2 corrects 'Guassian' to 'Gaussian' in the title, removes a stray quotation mark, and adds a Table 12 reference in Appendix C.1.3. The overall narrative and section order remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 12, groups Figures 6–7 on page 16, and consolidates Tables 9–11 on page 17. Figure 7 gains a caption explanation of the point colors. Existing figure imagery is retained.

improvement.justification: Table 12 makes the existing storage–quality trade-off easier to inspect by explicitly linking density settings to numerical outcomes. Figure 7's added color explanation and small editorial corrections improve clarity. These are limited reporting improvements; the method, experimental scope, and main conclusions remain unchanged.
